conventions.convention: The periodic cell is (R/LZ)^3 with normalized measure L⁻³dx, Fourier frequencies 2πk/L, dimensionless Sobolev weights, and unrestricted constant velocity mode. Physical kinetic energy uses unnormalized volume.
The row gradient is (∇u)ij = ∂jui; stress is −pI + 2μD(u), traction is σn, ν = μ/ρ₀, and kinematic pressure is p/ρ₀. Units are SI.

Weak velocities have actual weakly continuous H-valued representatives, strong initial traces, energy inequalities at every terminal time, and restart inequalities for starting times in one full-measure set together with zero.

On a nonempty bounded open vessel, H and V are respectively the L² and H₀¹ closures of compactly supported smooth solenoidal fields. No-slip is this closure condition; neither a pointwise trace nor identification with every solenoidal H₀¹ field is asserted. Spatial measure is unnormalized.

Rectangular pressure is a spacetime distribution with complex-linear bilinear test pairing and transpose-derivative signs. Its gauge is fixed by one real compact spatial test θ of integral one, requiring ⟨π,aθ⟩ = 0 for every temporal test a.
Periodic existence assumes Countable Choice; smooth consistency also assumes Dependent Choice; bounded existence and pressure carry the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice explicitly.

The periodic mechanical branch has no temperature variable. The rectangular insulated thermal branch is separate; identifying viscous dissipation with thermal heating requires an additional coupling assumption and common field/domain interface.

load_bearing.statement: Adopt the unforced, constant-positive-density and constant-positive-viscosity incompressible Newtonian model on the periodic cell, with classical stress −pI + 2μD(u) and, separately, the specified global periodic Leray–Hopf weak realization. No temperature variable, weak uniqueness, pressure regularity, or empirical universality is asserted.

For L > 0, constant ρ₀, μ > 0, ν = μ/ρ₀, and u₀ in the real solenoidal L² space with unrestricted mean, Countable Choice gives a global weak velocity of the adopted periodic model, with weak continuity, strong initial trace, the stated weak identity, all-time initial energy inequality and full-measure restart inequalities. Multiplication by ρ₀L³/2 gives the stated SI kinetic-energy inequalities. No pressure regularity, weak uniqueness, global smoothness, or empirical validity is asserted.

Adopt the constant-density, positive-viscosity, zero-force incompressible Newtonian model on a fixed nonempty bounded open vessel, using the specified solenoidal closure spaces and weak variational identity. No-slip means the H₀¹ closure condition, with no pointwise boundary trace or distributional pressure postulated.

For smooth divergence-free data in Hˢσ on the period-L three-torus, integer s ≥ 4, positive constant density and viscosity, and Countable and Dependent Choice, there is a positive smooth interval with a smooth velocity and smooth mean-zero kinematic pressure solving the full equation. Every global unforced periodic Leray–Hopf continuation with the same data agrees with that velocity throughout this interval.

For any nonempty bounded open three-dimensional vessel, the stated solenoidal closure spaces, constant ρ₀, μ > 0, u₀ ∈ H, AC and Countable Choice, the adopted unforced no-slip model has a global weak velocity with strong initial trace, the stated variational identity and initial/restart energy inequalities. Its SI kinetic energy obeys the displayed dissipation inequality; no pressure or pointwise wall trace is supplied.

On a finite open three-dimensional rectangle, with the stated closure spaces, positive constant density and viscosity, initial velocity in H, AC, Countable Choice and the specified continuous compact-test divergence inverse, there exist a global weak velocity with the stated energy inequalities and a real spacetime kinematic-pressure distribution satisfying the full momentum equation. Pressure is unique for that velocity under the fixed θ normalization; p = ρ₀π satisfies the physical momentum equation. No L² pressure, corner regularity or pointwise traction is asserted.
